👨‍🎓 About Me

Hi, I'm Zeshang Li. Welcome to my homepage! I received my Bachelor of Engineering from the University of International Relations. My research interests focus on reliable vision-language models and medical multimodal AI, and I am also open to exploring other research directions in AI. I am currently seeking MPhil opportunities and have an overall IELTS score of 7.0. Please feel free to reach out to discuss research ideas or potential opportunities.

📘 Selected Publications

Vision-Language Models

GEASS: Gated Evidence-Adaptive Selective Caption Trust for Vision-Language Models

Zeshang Li, Shuoyang Zhang

Submitted to CVM 2027 · arXiv

  • This work shows that self-generated captions can help or harm VLM predictions depending on the query, and introduces GEASS, a training-free decoding method that selectively uses caption evidence to reduce object hallucination.

Medical Multimodal AI

Hounsfield-CoT: Transferring 2D Medical MLLM Capabilities to 3D Volumetric Reasoning

Zhuoyuan Fu, Zeshang Li, Yiqiong Zhang, Hangui Lin, Yan Shu, Yan Li, Binyang Li, and Yaru Zhao

Accepted to BIBM 2026 · arXiv

  • This work introduces a slice-wise clinical reasoning dataset that enables a 2D-pretrained MLLM to approach native 3D model performance on volumetric medical images without 3D-specific pretraining.

🧭 Research Experiences

Transferring 2D Medical MLLM Capabilities to 3D Volumetric Reasoning

Jan 2026 – Jul 2026
  • Addressed the limited 3D reasoning capability of medical MLLMs that process volumetric scans as sequences of 2D slices and often struggle to integrate spatial information across slices. Constructed a slice-level chain-of-thought dataset that enables volumetric reasoning without a dedicated 3D encoder.
  • Designed a three-stage framework for individual slice analysis, integration of spatial information across adjacent slices, and differential reasoning. Built an automated pipeline to generate high-quality CoT question-answering data from existing 3D annotations, then applied LoRA-based supervised fine-tuning without changing the model architecture.
  • Evaluated the method on 3DRAD and DeepChestVQA, with consistent gains across all six 3DRAD tasks. Performance rose from 7.9% to 33.0% on Task 1 and from 7.7% to 24.4% on Task 2, approaching models with dedicated 3D encoders.

Phase-Specific Attention Intervention for Mitigating Object Hallucination (Thesis)

Feb 2026 – Jun 2026
  • Proposed a framework for reducing object hallucination in Think-Answer VLMs by separately analyzing the image description, reasoning, and final answer stages, then applying a targeted intervention at each stage without additional training or model parameters.
  • Developed a patch-level KL divergence metric to track changes in visual attention during reasoning. Identified object omission during image description, declining image attention during reasoning (0.058 to 0.027), and weak use of visual evidence in answer generation. Introduced Iterative Attention Grounding (IAG), Activation Union Map (AUM), and Visually-grounded Reasoning Guidance (VRG) based on these findings.
  • Improved HallusionBench accuracy from 61.2% to 64.8% and POPE from 85.2% to 86.9%. Ablations showed the reasoning-stage intervention had the largest impact: removing AUM reduced performance by 2.43 points.

Gated Evidence-Adaptive Selective Caption Trust for Vision-Language Models

Nov 2025 – May 2026
  • Found that feeding a VLM its own caption can reduce accuracy by about 10 points on HallusionBench for Qwen2.5-VL-3B. Proposed GEASS, a training-free, parameter-free logit-level module that decides per query whether and how much to trust a caption.
  • Built the GD-Probe diagnostic set (COCO, 850 paired questions) and showed caption utility varies by query: appending a caption helped global questions (+4.7 points) but hurt detail questions (−7.6 points).
  • Traced both effects to competition between the caption and image for attention, with the outcome depending on whether the caption covers the queried content. Target-region attention fell by 14–17% on detail questions.
  • Built a confidence gate, information-gain weight, and override guard from decoder-only signals. Restored detail accuracy above the no-caption baseline while preserving gains on global questions, and outperformed VCD/CODE across four VLMs and two benchmarks at approximately 2.3× decoding cost.

Fleming-VL: Universal Medical Visual Reasoning with Multimodal LLMs

Jun 2025 – Oct 2025
  • Built an automated synthesis pipeline using templates and LLMs for underrepresented 2D modalities (knee X-ray, fundus, and dermoscopy; Digital Knee X-ray, EyePACS, and PAD-UFES-20), turning sparse classification labels into reasoning-grounded VQA. Ablations identified this as the most impactful single data component (+6.8 on OmniMedVQA).
  • Constructed a medical video understanding dataset and the MedVideoBench evaluation benchmark from raw surgical and clinical videos, covering a modality with limited existing temporal data.
  • Ran SFT/GRPO fine-tuning across model scales and end-to-end 2D/3D/video evaluation. The 8B model reached state-of-the-art results among sub-10B open-source models: 73.3 average medical VQA, 90.2 medical Video-VQA, and 44.7 ROUGE-L on video summarization.
